newsitem.title: USA: Plane owners seek dialogue with new U.S. DoT head.
newsitem.headline: Plane owners seek dialogue with new U.S. DoT head.

text.p: The 340,000-member Aircraft Owners and Pilots Association (AOPA) on Friday asked for an improved relationship with the new Transportation Secretary designate, Rodney Slater.

AOPA president Phil Boyer said that as future aviation reforms are taken up, "the world's largest aviation organization hopes for a more open dialogue with the office of the secretary than we had during the president's first term."

He noted that general aviation represented 96 percent of the civil aviation fleet and served all of the nation's 18,343 landing facilities, against the two percent of airports served by major airlines on a scheduled basis.
"General aviation is a significant stakeholder in the national transportation system." Boyer said in a statement.
He added that "We look forward to working with the new secretary and ensuring he understands the vital role general aviation plays as part of our nation's transportation system."
